title: Jarren Duran shaves hair after slump with Boston Red Sox
seoTitle: Jarren Duran shaves hair after slump with Boston Red Sox
subtitle: The baseball player seeks to regain his form after posting numbers below expectations in recent seasons.
excerpt: Jarren Duran adopted a new look to try to overcome a rough patch with the Boston Red Sox and help the team chase a playoff spot.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Boston Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran made a drastic change by shaving almost all of his long hair to celebrate his 30th birthday on Saturday, September 5. The makeover comes at a time of a sharp decline in the athlete’s performance over the past two seasons. With the new look, the player hopes to recapture his good form and help his team in the hunt for a playoff berth.

Makeover after a performance dip

Duran was known for his long hair, but he opted for an extremely short, buzz‑cut style. In baseball, players are often superstitious and turn to drastic changes to try to attract better luck. The expectation that the new look would produce immediate results, however, was not met in Sunday’s game against the Orioles, when the athlete finished the contest without a hit in four at‑bats and struck out.

Stats point to a tough stretch this season

The numbers show that regaining strong performance requires more than a haircut. Duran is posting a batting average of just .196 over the last 30 games, which drops to .137 in his past 15 matchups and falls to .111 in his most recent seven games. The decline has been continuous since 2024, when he posted an OPS of .834 with 14 triples, 21 home runs and 34 stolen bases. In 2025 those figures fell to a .774 OPS, 13 triples, 16 home runs and 24 steals. This season his OPS has plunged to .614, with only four triples, though he still has 19 home runs and 18 successful steals out of 22 attempts.

Fierce competition for Boston’s outfield spots

Duran’s reduced playing time also stems from strong competition on the Red Sox roster. The outfield currently features Wilyer Abreu in right field, while Roman Anthony has returned from injury to take on a key role in the club’s plans. Ceddanne Rafaela, who is temporarily injured, is expected to reclaim center field once he’s healthy, further lessening the need for Duran to start daily.

Player’s future and team plans

During the previous trade window, Duran was considered a trade candidate as Boston appeared to need to move an outfielder. Since no deal materialized, the team kept him on the roster through the end of the season before recalibrating its long‑term strategy. The player hopes that the lighter feeling on his shoulders, courtesy of the new look, will help improve his situation on the field.

With information from Heavy.com.
